analysis.title: Commodity Views: 2027 Outlook: Adapting to Rough Waters
key_insights: GS recommends a positive commodities allocation. Its base case of further energy price moderation implies near-zero BCOM total returns from now to end-2027 (after +26% YTD), but tactical and structural drivers support commodities as a hedge and diversifier.
Base case 2027 average Brent is $88/bbl and European TTF gas is 45 EUR/MWh, as Mideast supply keeps adapting. Current levels are Brent $93 and TTF 87 EUR/MWh.

GS attributes the November selloff in energy and copper to shifts in sentiment and near-term Mideast escalation risk, not physical fundamentals. It estimates the Brent risk premium fell from $27 on the Friday before the midterms to a few dollars, which it says makes entry more attractive for hedging.

Persian Gulf crude exports recovered to near 2025 levels in September and the global oil market likely returned to surplus in October. GS expects ship-to-ship transfers and pipeline additions to lift Mideast oil output to 1.1mb/d above 2025 levels on average in 2027.

Supply adaptation has worked less well for refined products, LNG, aluminium feedstock and fertilizers. These fuels are harder to transfer ship to ship, and refining, aluminium smelting and LNG liquefaction capacity is not fully repaired from strikes.

Tanker market adaptation to Mideast shipping risk accounts for about 3/4 of the ~$20/bbl y/y rise in the global average crude freight rate (28-day MA). GS expects freight to stay high while ship-to-ship transfers and the US blockade of Iran persist, and the cost passes through to retail fuel prices.

Upside energy scenario: Brent could pass $130 in early 2027 and average about $120 in 2027 if Gulf output averages 2.5mb/d below 2025. US wholesale diesel could reach new highs of $230 around year-end if refining output falls a further 3mb/d.

TTF could approach 150 EUR/MWh in 2027Q1 if Gulf LNG exports run at 25-30% of pre-war levels and winter is 1 std. dev. colder. If Gulf LNG stalls at about 35% of pre-war levels through end-2027, TTF would average 104 EUR/MWh in 2027.

Since the Iran war began, equities and especially bonds have been unusually sensitive to energy prices. GS says a renewed supply shock in 2027 could mean lower bond prices (as in 2026) and lower equities (as in 2022), with commodities providing diversification. The 1-month Brent/10Y correlation has turned negative since late September as AI and risk-asset volatility dominate.
In every 12-month period over six decades when both equities and bonds had negative real returns, gold or broad commodities delivered positive real returns.

Agriculture: BCOM Agriculture is up 10% YTD with upside risk from the Iran and Russia-Ukraine conflicts, a likely record-strength El Niño, and possible food export restrictions. Hormuz-linked trade is about 1/3 of global fertilizer exports and the Black Sea is 15-20% of global grain trade.
Weather risks: low European river levels (Danube, Rhine) constrain shipping and power. El Niño threatens West Africa cocoa in 2026Q4 and Vietnam robusta coffee in 2027Q1.

Trade: long EBOB Jun27 European gasoline. Refiners shifting to diesel and jet tighten gasoline, and low gasoline margins leave room for upside. Expected total return is 20% in the base case and 62% on renewed escalation, with a 4% loss if refining capacity is restored and Gulf crude supply beats base by 1.4mb/d.
Trade: long 2027Q1 TTF call spreads to hedge a tight European winter, given low inventories and the recent risk premium liquidation.

Copper: LME copper forecast at $15,600/t by Dec27 (+13% from spot) on electrification, data centers, AI and constrained mine supply. US tariff ambiguity and China scrap-to-cathode substitution have cut ex-US stocks to seasonal lows. Near-term downside risks are less US tariff ambiguity and weak recovery in AI-related investor length.

Long Dec27 LME copper / short Dec27 LME aluminium is reiterated. Aluminium is forecast to fall to $2,600 by Dec27 as Indonesian output rises to about 4% of global supply by end-2027 (from 1% at end-2025). The spread should be more resilient to macro-driven position cuts than outright copper.

Gold forecast cut to $4,650/toz for Dec27 (from $4,800), +16% from spot. GS economists now expect a third 25bp Fed hike in March 2027 after a second in December 2026. Rate hikes should weigh on private gold demand into early 2027 despite central bank buying, and demand should recover once the Fed starts easing in December 2027.
Long TTF Summer 29 puts are recommended as a short on 2029 European gas, since the 2025-26 LNG FID wave leaves post-2027 LNG balances oversupplied.
GS thinks the US midterm results are more likely to delay than derail US data center capacity growth, so copper investor positioning should partly recover.

sector_views.rationale: Supply-shock hedge for bond-equity portfolios and diversifier given concentrated supply and heightened disruption risk, with risk premia now lower.
Base case is further price moderation (Brent $88 in 2027), but with asymmetric upside risk from renewed Mideast escalation and a cold winter.
Copper is favored on constrained supply and AI, electrification and stockpiling demand, while aluminium is expected to go into surplus.
Structural central bank gold buying, with near-term pressure from Fed hikes and private demand returning once easing starts in December 2027.
Conflict, fertilizer, biofuel and El Niño risks skew prices upward.

trade_ideas.description: Long BCOM (Bloomberg Commodity index) as a supply-shock hedge for bond-equity portfolios
trade_ideas.rationale: Concentrated supply and high but unpredictable disruption risk make broad commodity exposure an attractive hedge.

trade_ideas.description: Long EBOB Jun27 European gasoline futures
trade_ideas.rationale: Refiners shifting output to diesel and jet reduce gasoline supply, and low gasoline margins leave room for sharp upside on geopolitical disruption.
trade_ideas.risk: A 4% loss if damaged refining capacity returns and Gulf upstream supply beats base by 1.4mb/d in 2027.

trade_ideas.description: Long call spreads on TTF European gas 2027Q1
trade_ideas.rationale: Reescalation cutting LNG supply plus a colder-than-average winter with low inventories could send TTF sharply higher.
trade_ideas.risk: Warm winter or faster Gulf LNG recovery.

trade_ideas.rationale: Structural central bank bid provides a floor through the Fed hiking cycle, and easing from late 2027 should bring back private investor demand.
trade_ideas.risk: Further Fed hikes weigh on private demand into early 2027.

trade_ideas.description: Long Dec-27 LME copper, short Dec-27 LME aluminium
trade_ideas.rationale: Copper faces mine supply constraints, electrification demand and low ex-US stocks, while Indonesian smelting pushes aluminium into surplus.
trade_ideas.risk: Lower US tariff ambiguity or weak recovery in AI-related investor length.

trade_ideas.rationale: Longer-term LNG balances look oversupplied as the 2025-26 LNG FID wave adds post-2027 supply.

risk_factors: Renewed Mideast escalation, including tanker attacks near Hormuz or damage to energy infrastructure, could push Brent above $130 and diesel to $230.
A cold winter combined with low European gas inventories and weak Gulf LNG exports could take TTF near 150 EUR/MWh in 2027Q1.
Near-term copper downside from reduced US tariff ambiguity or a lackluster recovery in AI-related investor length.
Additional Fed hikes or a turn in the AI cycle could cut macro-driven positioning.
Downside oil scenario: Gulf upstream supply beats base by 1.4mb/d and damaged refining capacity returns, producing a 4% loss on the gasoline trade.
El Niño, European river-level drought and food export restrictions could lift agricultural prices.
Downside risks to global GDP and employment, with slower earnings growth, could hit equities and bonds in a supply shock.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 shows the estimated Brent risk premium dropping sharply, from $27 on the Friday before the midterms to a few dollars.

Exhibit 6 shows 2027Q1 TTF scenarios: base case (rising winter supply) 65, low winter supply 102, 1 std. dev. colder 106 and 147 across supply cases, 1 std. dev. warmer 41 and 58, versus forwards at 85 EUR/MWh.
Exhibit 16 shows BCOM returning 26% YTD, 2% for the balance of 2026, -2% in 2027 and -1% from now to end-2027, with energy at 1% and precious metals at 12% now to end-2027.
Exhibit 17 lists GS forecasts: Brent $93 now to $88 in 2027, TTF 87 to 45 EUR/MWh, LME copper 13,821 to 15,400 in 2027, LME aluminum 3,085 to 2,700.
vol_and_positioning: Recent AI-related equity volatility has reduced copper investor length, and GS expects positioning to at least partly recover.
Long copper/short aluminium is seen as less exposed to macro-driven position reductions (an AI cycle turn, more Fed hikes) than outright long copper.
Risk premium liquidation in energy has made gasoline and TTF call spread entries more attractive, and a hawkish Fed outlook weighs on private investor gold positioning through early 2027.
geopolitical: US-Iran war and Hormuz: tanker attacks near Hormuz have picked up and a lasting diplomatic breakthrough is uncertain. The US blockade of Iranian tankers continues.
Mideast diplomatic efforts are now top of mind for markets, while Persian Gulf crude exports have recovered to near 2025 levels.
Russia-Ukraine conflict constrains refining output and Black Sea grain exports.

US-China competition for refined copper and wider geopolitical fragmentation raise disruption risk, citing the 2022 Russian gas shock, last year's Chinese rare earths shock and this year's Hormuz shock.
US midterm elections results are seen delaying rather than derailing US data center growth.

tension_points.bull_case: Renewed Mideast escalation or a cold winter could send Brent above $130 and TTF near 150 EUR/MWh, and a lower risk premium makes hedge entry cheaper.
tension_points.bear_case: Base case has Mideast supply continuing to adapt, with Gulf crude exports near 2025 levels and the oil market in surplus, so Brent falls to $88 and TTF to 45 EUR/MWh in 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A lasting diplomatic breakthrough, Gulf output beating base by 1.4mb/d with refining capacity restored, or a warmer-than-average winter would invalidate the upside hedges.

tension_points.bull_case: Electrification, data center and AI demand with constrained mine supply and low ex-US stocks lift LME copper to $15,600/t by Dec27.
tension_points.bear_case: Less US tariff ambiguity and a lackluster recovery in AI-related investor length could cause near-term downside to the forecast.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A reduction in US tariff ambiguity or a lackluster recovery in AI-related investor length.

tension_points.bull_case: Structural central bank buying, including China's, and Fed easing from December 2027 revive private investor demand, lifting gold to $4,650/toz.
tension_points.bear_case: A hawkish Fed with hikes in December 2026 and March 2027 weighs on private investor positioning into early 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Fed easing arriving later than December 2027, or central bank buying slowing.
